# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `tools/fa-clip/` — the native macOS pasteboard helper (gh-2040): a plain
  `NSPasteboard` reader (`fa-clip <png|jpeg|tiff>` → bytes on stdout, exit
  2 = flavor absent), built by `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` into the macOS
  CLI bundles (`bundle/bin/fa-clip`, per-arch) and shipped beside the `fa`
  binary — install.sh, install_local.sh and the self-update swap all copy
  it. The CLI resolves it relative to its own executable, never PATH; a
  missing/broken helper degrades to the named pasteboard-unavailable path.
  NEVER reintroduce the AppleScript/Apple Events clipboard transport
  (`osascript` is grep-gated out of `bin/` + `lib/src/cli/` —
  test/cli/fa_clip_helper_test.dart); the TCC «access data from other
  apps» dialog class must stay dead. macOS text reads stay on `pbpaste`
  (already prompt-free — documented split, gh-2040 AC4).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics. Self-signal immunity
  (gh-1763): POSIX scripts are delivered from a per-exec private temp
  file (`sh -c '. "$1"' sh <script>` — prelude restores `sh -c`
  positional-param parity, so `$0`/`$#`/exit codes/`set -e`/stdin are
  unchanged; legacy `sh -c <command>` fallback when the temp dir cannot
  be created) so the wrapper argv never carries the script body —
  `pkill -f <pat>` inside a command cannot match its own shell; a
  provisioned-once guard (`lib/src/env/bash_guard_io.dart`) puts
  `pkill`/`killall` PATH shims at the head of PATH plus a `kill()`
  prelude function, both excluding the harness pid chain + process group
  (exported as `FA_PROTECTED_PIDS`, overridable per exec via
  `ShellExecOptions.env` for tests) and the invoking shell, while
  legitimate victims stay killable; Windows keeps `cmd /c` verbatim.
  Residual caveat: shapes the shim cannot model — output modes
  (`-c`, `-v`, `-l`, `-a`, `--count`, any other long option), a signal
  spelled after the pattern, extra operands, or a selection pgrep
  rejects — exec the real, unshimed binary and are NOT covered by the
  exemption (keep the pattern away from the harness cmdline in those
  spellings).
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  gh-1934 (413-proof sessions): image blocks OUTSIDE the kept region —
  first seen before the LAST renumbering boundary — evict to
  `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders (payload-only, JSONL
  byte-identical); kept-region images ride on under the normal caps; the 413 recovery ladder
  (`agent_loop_image_recovery.dart` + `image_recovery.dart`, bounded at
  2 passes per response, each 413 halving the session's adaptive
  `images.maxBytesPerRequest`) drops the oldest images (pass 1), then
  strips ALL images including the current message (pass 2, latched
  session-wide), carrying the `[images] recovered from 413:` notice +
  model-visible note; classification lives in `image_overflow.dart`
  (`isPayloadTooLargeError`), surface wording in `image_drop_ux.dart`
  (`ImageDropReason.evicted`).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape (no eviction, no ladder). `agent_loop.dart` applies it in
  `_buildRequestContext` after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing
  repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — the FinalizeGate contract +
  TaskLedger (gh-1412): near-miss elimination for unattended runs. In
  unattended/bench mode the CLI system prompt appends the `finalize_gate`
  contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, composed in
  `agent_cli_prompt.dart`; interactive modes never carry it) — before any
  final summary the agent re-quotes every explicit requirement as a
  checklist, verifies each item with a real command against the produced
  state, and fixes every unmet item. The clock is the harness's
  (gh-1646): the contract says work to the wall — the time-left notices
  report the remaining budget, and while work remains the next
  compliant action is another approach, not a final answer (the run is
  interrupted automatically at the deadline). Feasibility is checked at
  commitment time (gh-1670): before any cost-dominating step (from-source
  builds, large downloads, brute-force searches) the contract teaches
  estimating the duration against the time-left notices and switching to
  a cheaper satisfying strategy — or, when none fits, the next-best
  partial — rather than gambling the window on a known-infeasible path.
  Conformance claims are the self-certification blind spot (gh-1834):
  when the final claim includes parity/conformance to a reference or
  specification (any domain), a "verified" item counts only with
  negative and combination checks — refused incompatible options,
  empty/corrupt inputs, boundary values, must-NOT-work cases — alongside
  happy paths; a blanket "everything matches" is not verified (prompt
  step 2.6, conditional: tasks with no conformance claim are
  unchanged).
  The loop parses
  the final answer's `task-ledger` fenced block (`parseTaskLedger`,
  last block wins) and emits `TaskLedgerEvent`; hosts persist the hidden
  `task_ledger` custom record (CLI: `agent_event_handler.dart` →
  `_onTaskLedger` in `trajectory_commands.dart` — the `appendCustomEntry`
  lives there, redacted through the host pipeline — wired through
  `handleAgentEvent`'s nullable `onTaskLedger` callback; unset keeps
  interactive sessions ledger-less), the wire protocol carries `task_ledger`
  (golden fixture +
  web client `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`), and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds
  the latest ledger into `snapshot.taskLedger` (legacy sessions degrade to
  null). The bench summaries render near-miss proximity from the synced
  session logs: terminal-bench adds a per-task `checklist` table column,
  harbor a `Checklist coverage` block — both parse the LAST `task_ledger`
  record (`pass`/`fixed` count as verified; no ledger → `checklist: none`).
  AC5: a declined `request_secret` in unattended mode carries the
  credential-hunt nudge (`credentialHuntNudge`;
  `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended`, keyed by the CLI on the LIVE approval
  mode so a runtime `/approval` switch flips it).
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). gh-1835: a foreground bash call still
  running after `waiting.autoBackgroundSeconds` (default 60; 0 = kill
  switch) is auto-backgrounded — CONVERTED, never restarted (it already

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 2051
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/2051
- **Title**: gh-2050 [daily-publish] cli leg failed
- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +198
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-11-03T07:40:18Z
- **Updated**: 2026-11-03T07:44:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #2050
### Root Cause
The daily-publish `cli` leg resolves its release tag (`latest+1`) at dispatch, but the concurrent mobile leg + tag train create and **publish** that same tag ~25 min after dispatch (v1.0.685: draft 05:22:46Z, published 05:44:52Z) while the serialized self-hosted macOS builds finish ~68 min in. The gh-2042 immutability gate (`scripts/release_asset_gate.sh`) then correctly refuses the leg's now-unattached `fa-macos-*` assets on the PUBLISHED release → exit 1 → daily red leg (run 41583268061).

### Fix
- `scripts/release_asset_gate.sh`: added caller-declared pre-stage policy `RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1` — the PUBLISHED + unattached-`fa-*` verdict becomes a loud whole-call skip (`::warning::`, exit 0, nothing uploaded, no twin create, no flip). All-or-nothing, so `latest-mac.yml` can never land alone on a release whose zips were skipped. Default stays the gh-2042 AC1 loud refusal; exact `1` required (fail-closed).
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`: only the `release-macos` desktop attach step opts in; the CLI-tar/extension attaches keep the refusal (they carry REQUIRED release assets).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: `## Unreleased` entry.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 6 new tests failed before the fix — `test/release_asset_gate_test.dart` (policy skip verdict, mixed-list whole-call skip, draft path untouched, opt-in discipline for non-`1` values, workflow env pin) and `test/release_publish_immutability_test.dart` (attach-or-create end-to-end: green leg, zero mutation). All pass now; every existing gh-2042 refusal pin untouched.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext,llm` → **13410 passed, 13 skipped** (macOS-only/machine-gated), 0 failures.

### Notes
- The skipped desktop assets self-heal: the next daily leg pre-stages the **next** version's draft with fresh assets (v1.0.683–685 shipped no desktop DMGs anyway — the leg was red for unrelated infra causes those days).
- Architectural gap observed, not fixed here (owner decision): the mac desktop pre-stage window is ~25 min vs ~66 min builds, so the feed will strand on any raced day — a decoupled desktop update channel is worth a follow-up ticket.
- The sibling mobile leg has the same theoretical exposure (its `fa.ipa` is `fa-*`); left untouched — no observed failure and its store assets are non-required refreshers.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release asset immutability gate (gh-2042, AC1): the single attach path for
# `fa-*` assets onto a GitHub Release.
#
# The v1.0.680 incident: the daily build-macos train resolved a tag whose
# release was ALREADY PUBLISHED (the same-tag convergence race — the tag
# train published while the daily train's slow self-hosted legs were still
# building) and re-attached fresh fa-macos-arm64 assets ~2-3h AFTER the
# signed SHA256SUMS was attached. The manifest never re-ran, so every
# `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on the train failed for every
# macOS-arm64 user. A published release must be IMMUTABLE for `fa-*`
# assets: the signed manifest vouches for exactly the bytes that were on
# the release when release-provenance signed it.
#
# Verdicts (per call, all-or-nothing — a partial attach would still drift
# the manifest):
#   release missing        → allow (the caller lazy-drafts first; a raw
#                            upload to a missing release errors loudly)
#   release is a DRAFT     → attach everything --clobber (the gh-1801 flow,
#                            unchanged: publish stays provenance-owned)
#   release is PUBLISHED   → for every listed asset:
#                              - name already attached → immutable SKIP
#                                (the release-twin binaries re-run: same
#                                tag commit, asset already shipped)
#                              - name not attached, matches `fa-*` →
#                                REFUSE the whole call with a loud
#                                ::error:: (post-publish attach must
#                                target a DRAFT / next-version or re-run
#                                release-provenance for the tag) — OR,
#                                when the caller declares
#                                RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1, SKIP the
#                                whole call with a loud ::warning::
#                                instead (gh-2050: the daily pre-stager
#                                legs' draft window closed — a sibling
#                                train published the tag while they were
#                                still building; nothing uploads, nothing
#                                mutates, the next daily leg pre-stages
#                                the next version)
#                              - name not attached, NOT fa-* → attach
#                                (store AAB/IPA/APK + DMG refreshers are
#                                deliberately not provenance-covered,
#                                see scripts/release_required_assets.txt)
#   anything undeterminable (API blip, unparseable verdict) → fail CLOSED
#
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) are NOT fa-* assets: release-provenance's raw
# `gh release upload` of the manifest is the sanctioned post-publish
# remediation (re-hash the current bytes, re-sign) and stays outside this
# gate by design (gh-2042 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_asset_gate.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN,
#      RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP (gh-2050 pre-stage skip — exact "1").
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_asset_gate.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::release_asset_gate.sh called with zero assets for $tag — a caller bug: resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

err=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$err"' EXIT
state_json=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft,assets 2>"$err") || {
  if grep -qi "not found" "$err"; then
    # Release absent: the attach path lazily creates the DRAFT first
    # (release_lazy_draft.sh / the create in release_attach_or_create.sh).
    # Attempt the upload — a still-missing release errors loudly in gh.
    for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
      gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
    done
    echo "✅ gate: release $tag absent — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) (draft-first flow)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::cannot determine the release state of $tag ($(cat "$err")) — refusing to attach (gh-2042 fail-closed: an undeterminable verdict must never mutate a release)" >&2
  exit 1
}

if printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -e '.isDraft == false' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # PUBLISHED — the immutability contract.
  attached=$(printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -r '.assets[].name')
  refused=()
  skipped=()
  uploadable=()
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    name=$(basename "$asset")
    if printf '%s\n' "$attached" | grep -qxF "$name"; then
      skipped+=("$name")
    elif [[ "$name" == fa-* ]]; then
      refused+=("$name")
    else
      uploadable+=("$asset")
    fi
  done
  if [ "${#refused[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    # gh-2050: the caller-declared PRE-STAGE policy. The daily build-macos /
    # build-mobile legs are next-tag-draft PRE-STAGERS (their DMGs/zips/
    # latest-mac.yml are clobber-refresher assets, not publish blockers —
    # release_required_assets.txt). When the sibling train publishes the
    # derived tag while the slow legs are still building (the v1.0.685
    # daily run: draft 05:22:46, published 05:44:52, mac leg attached
    # 06:28:53), the pre-stager's draft window is simply closed — its only
    # honest action is a loud whole-call skip; the next daily leg pre-stages
    # the NEXT version's draft with fresh assets. Exact "1" or the default
    # refusal below stays armed (fail-closed).
    if [ "${RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP:-}" = "1" ]; then
      echo "::warning::release $tag is PUBLISHED — pre-stage skip (RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1, gh-2050): the unattached fa-* asset(s) [${refused[*]}] cannot attach (gh-2042 AC1: a published release is immutable for fa-* assets; its signed SHA256SUMS vouches for the bytes already on it). NOTHING was uploaded — the whole call is skipped, non-fa-* assets included (a latest-mac.yml landing alone would serve the mac update feed a manifest of missing files). A sibling train published this tag while this leg was still building; the next daily leg pre-stages the next version's draft with fresh assets. Landing these assets on THIS tag needs a human-sanctioned post-publish remediation: attach, then re-run the release-provenance sign job for the tag (it re-hashes the current assets and re-signs)." >&2
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "::error::release $tag is PUBLISHED — attaching unattached fa-* asset(s) [${refused[*]}] would invalidate its signed SHA256SUMS (gh-2042 AC1: a published release is immutable for fa-* assets). Remediate by re-running the release-provenance job for the tag (it re-hashes the current assets and re-signs), or target the next-version DRAFT instead." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  for name in "${skipped[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$name" ] || continue
    echo "✅ gate: $name already on the published release $tag — immutable skip (gh-2042)"
  done
  for asset in "${uploadable[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$asset" ] || continue
    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
    echo "✅ gate: $(basename "$asset") attached to $tag (not provenance-covered)"
  done
  exit 0
fi

if printf '%s' "$state_json" | jq -e '.isDraft == true' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # DRAFT — the normal pre-publish attach (unchanged since gh-1801).
  for asset in "${assets[@]}"; do
    gh release upload "$tag" "$asset" --clobber --repo "$repo"
  done
  echo "✅ gate: ${#assets[@]} asset(s) attached to draft $tag — publish stays provenance-owned"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::unparseable release state for $tag — refusing to attach (gh-2042 fail-closed)" >&2
exit 1

uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          path: dmgs
          pattern: Fa-macos-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        run: ls -laR dmgs/

      - name: Merge macOS auto-update manifest
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --user pyyaml
          chmod +x scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh
          scripts/merge-mac-update-manifest.sh dmgs dmgs/latest-mac.yml
          cat dmgs/latest-mac.yml

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
          # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
          # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
          # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          # gh-2050: this attach is the daily NEXT-TAG-DRAFT pre-stager (its
          # DMGs/zips/latest-mac.yml are clobber-refresher assets, not
          # publish blockers — release_required_assets.txt). When the
          # sibling train publishes the derived tag while the serialized
          # self-hosted mac builds are still running (the v1.0.685 daily
          # run: draft 05:22:46, published 05:44:52, this leg attached
          # 06:28:53), the gate's PUBLISHED refusal would red this leg
          # daily. RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1 turns that verdict into a
          # loud whole-call skip — nothing uploads, nothing mutates (gh-2042
          # AC1 intact; the gate's default remains the refusal), and the
          # next daily leg pre-stages the next version's draft with fresh
          # assets. The build-macos-cli / build-extension attaches below do
          # NOT get this policy: their fa-* assets are REQUIRED release
          # assets the tag train ships, so their verdict must stay loud.
          RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP: '1'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          DMGS=$(ls dmgs/*.dmg 2>/dev/null || true)
          ZIPS=$(ls dmgs/*-mac.zip 2>/dev/null || true)
          MANIFEST="dmgs/latest-mac.yml"
          echo "DMGs to upload: $DMGS"
          echo "ZIPs to upload: $ZIPS"

          STABLE_COPIES=()
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            # Skip no-sandbox zips from the auto-update stable names; the
            # sandboxed build is the default update feed.
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64-mac.zip")
            elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
              cp "$zip" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64-mac.zip"
              STABLE_COPIES+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64-mac.zip")
            fi
          done

          # Extract the raw binary from the .app bundle and upload it as the
          # plain asset name (fa-macos-arm64 / fa-macos-x64) so `fa update`
          # and direct downloads work without knowing the version suffix.
          for zip in $ZIPS; do
            base=$(basename "$zip")
            if [[ "$base" == *nosandbox* ]]; then
              continue
            fi
            unzip -qo "$zip" -d /tmp/fa-extract >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            BIN="/tmp/fa-extract/Fa.app/Contents/MacOS/Fa"
            if [ -f "$BIN" ]; then
              if [[ "$base" == *arm64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-arm64")
              elif [[ "$base" == *x86_64* ]]; then
                cp "$BIN" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64"
                ASSETS+=("dmgs/fa-macos-x64")
              fi
              chmod +x "dmgs/fa-macos-arm64" "dmgs/fa-macos-x64" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            rm -rf /tmp/fa-extract
          done
          ASSETS=($DMGS $ZIPS $MANIFEST "${STABLE_COPIES[@]}")

          # Notes come from the CHANGELOG section for this version, with a
          # conventional-commit fallback (issue #282: no more filler
          # bodies); the install hints stay as a footer.
          bash scripts/release_notes.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" > release-notes.md || true
          printf '\n## Installation\n- **macOS**: Download the DMG for your architecture (`arm64` for Apple Silicon, `x86_64` for Intel) and drag Fa.app to Applications. In-app updates use the ZIP + latest-mac.yml feed.\n- **Linux**: Download tar.gz, extract and run the `bundle/fa` binary.\n- **Windows**: Download zip, extract and run the `fa.exe`.\n' >> release-notes.md

          # Attach-or-create (issue #282 E3 + review of #294): idempotent
          # against the view->create race - a lost race uploads into the
          # winner's release instead of failing - and the create stamps an
          # ownership marker into the draft body, so the guard step below

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: gate-guarded attach + (servable DRAFT-only) publish + latest
  # gh-2042 (AC1): every upload passes the immutability gate — on a
  # PUBLISHED release an unattached fa-* asset refuses the whole call loud,
  # an already-attached one skips, and non-fa store/DMG refreshers keep
  # their clobber-refresh contract. Drafts attach exactly as before.
  # gh-2042 (review): ONE call for the WHOLE list — the gate's contract is
  # per-call all-or-nothing ("refuse before any upload"), so per-asset
  # invocation would judge each asset against its own release-view
  # snapshot (N round-trips, a wider draft→published TOCTOU window, and a
  # partial mutation when an early benign asset uploads before a later
  # fa-* refusal).
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "${assets[@]}"
  # Latest policy (#282 + gh-1801 rework + gh-2042): publish + latest ONLY
  # when the release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate) — AND it is
  # still a DRAFT (the provenance-flip recovery window). A PUBLISHED
  # release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that
  # would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade.
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    case "$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo false)" in
      true)
        gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"
        # gh-1899: same duplicate-tag race as the tag train — a twin draft
        # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
        # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
        # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.
        bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_dedupe.sh" "$tag" \
          || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
        ;;
      *)
        echo "release $tag is already published — publish/latest flip skipped (gh-2042: latest never moves backwards; the signed SHA256SUMS re-upload is release-provenance's job)"
        ;;
    esac
  else
    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi
}

# fa-update servability = the signed checksums are on the release. Every
# fa-* archive alone is NOT enough: `fa update` fetches SHA256SUMS(.sig)
# and aborts when either is missing (bin/self_manage.dart).
release_serves_fa_update() {
  local names
  names=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
  printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -qE '^SHA256SUMS(\.sig)?$'
}

if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to existing release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: prepared notes (CHANGELOG section / conventional-commit fallback)
# plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
notes="release-notes.md"
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)} -->"
[ -s "$notes" ] || printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" > "$notes"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >> "$notes"

# A `gh release create` for a MISSING tag mints a lightweight API tag:
# no push event → no ci.yml tag run → no publish/binaries (the v0.1.408
# silent class, issue #597). If the ref is absent, mint it as an
# ANNOTATED tag and push it with the PAT the job already carries
# (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos) so the tag CI fires. The mint
# itself (GH_TOKEN guard, persisted-checkout-extraheader strip, push,
# train-start verification) lives in scripts/release_tag_mint.sh —
# gh-2026: the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 minted pushes rode actions/checkout's
# persisted GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader (it outranks the URL credentials),
# GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes, no tag run
# ever existed on those refs, and the drafts rotted behind green legs.
# A mint whose train does not start now fails loud BEFORE any draft is
# created, so the leg goes red and the failure-path draft guard has
# nothing to reclaim.
# Gate on the DEFINITE missing verdict (ls-remote --exit-code rc 2):
# sandboxes without an origin remote fatal with 128 — indeterminable
# falls through to the plain create path (test fixtures rely on it).
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# Bare vX.Y.Z title (#282): matches the tag, matches pub.dev. gh-1801
# rework: the create is DRAFT-ONLY. Whatever this leg resolved
# (AAB/IPA/store APKs, DMGs/zips) is not the signed provenance `fa update`
# demands — a leg that arrives first must never publish the release, let
# alone flag it latest (threads 2/6). The draft is ownership-stamped (the
# marker below) so this job's draft lifecycle guard reclaims it on
# failure; the tag-run binaries job attaches the CLI assets into it and
# release-provenance (ci.yml) publishes + flags latest once SHA256SUMS.sig
# is on board.
if gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes" \
  "${assets[@]}"; then
  echo "✅ created draft release $tag with ${#assets[@]} asset(s) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi

# E3 idempotency: the create may have lost the view→create race — the
# winner's release now exists. Attach instead of failing (a failing
# create would fire the guard against the winner's in-flight draft).
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ lost the create race — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to the concurrently created release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::release create for $tag failed and no concurrent release appeared — see the step log above" >&2
exit 1

path: artifacts/

      - name: Download god APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-god
          path: artifacts/

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        run: ls -laR artifacts/

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — the
          # attach-or-create script builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN
          # is set; without it `git push ""` died with "fatal: bad
          # repository ''" (2026-10-22 v1.0.626 mobile leg).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          AAB=$(find artifacts -name "*.aab" -type f | head -1)
          IPA=$(find artifacts -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          STORE_APK=$(find artifacts -name "app-store-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          GOD_APK=$(find artifacts -name "app-god-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          echo "AAB: $AAB"
          echo "IPA: $IPA"
          echo "store APK: $STORE_APK"
          echo "god APK: $GOD_APK"

          ASSETS=()
          [ -n "$AAB" ] && ASSETS+=("$AAB")
          [ -n "$IPA" ] && ASSETS+=("$IPA")
          [ -n "$STORE_APK" ] && ASSETS+=("$STORE_APK")
          [ -n "$GOD_APK" ] && ASSETS+=("$GOD_APK")

          # Notes come from the CHANGELOG section for this version, with a
          # conventional-commit fallback (issue #282: no more filler
          # bodies); the install hints stay as a footer.
          bash scripts/release_notes.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" > release-notes.md || true
          printf '\n## Installation\n- **Android**: Download the AAB and upload to Play Store, or use `flutter install`.\n- **Android god flavor (sideload only)**: install the god APK directly — see https://fa1.dev/android.\n- **iOS**: Download the IPA and upload to TestFlight via Xcode or Transporter.\n- **macOS**: Download the DMG from the macOS build workflow.\n' >> release-notes.md

          # Attach-or-create (issue #282 E3 + review of #294): idempotent
          # against the view->create race - a lost race uploads into the
          # winner's release instead of failing - and the create stamps an
          # ownership marker into the draft body, so the guard step below
          # only ever deletes THIS job's draft, never the macOS leg's
          # mid-upload draft on the same derived tag.
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "${ASSETS[@]}"

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2050): the daily-publish `cli` leg red-failed daily when its
  macOS attach arrived after a sibling train had already PUBLISHED the
  derived tag (the same-tag convergence race: mobile leg drafts + the tag
  train publishes ~25 min after dispatch while the serialized self-hosted
  mac builds need ~66 min — v1.0.685: draft 05:22:46, published 05:44:52,
  mac leg attached 06:28:53). `scripts/release_asset_gate.sh` gains a
  caller-declared pre-stage policy — `RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1` —
  that turns the PUBLISHED+unattached-fa-* verdict into a loud whole-call
  skip (`::warning::`, exit 0, nothing uploaded, no twin create, no flip;
  all-or-nothing so `latest-mac.yml` can never land alone on a release
  whose zips were skipped). The default stays the gh-2042 AC1 loud
  refusal; only build-macos.yml's `release-macos` desktop attach opts in
  (its DMGs/zips/manifest are clobber-refresher pre-stage assets, not
  publish blockers), the CLI-tar/extension attaches keep the refusal (they
  carry REQUIRED release assets). The stranded desktop feed self-heals:
  the next daily leg pre-stages the next version's draft with fresh
  assets.

  everything when its budget never exhausted, swallowing the live tail

`RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1` converts only the `refused > 0` verdict into a whole-call skip. This matches the gh-2042 non-fa refresher contract as written, and the PR description declares the "can never land alone" invariant for the refused case — the implementation matches what is declared, so this is not blocking. Today the policy cannot affect it (the check only lives inside the `refused > 0` branch), so the lazy draft-first flow still attaches — the pre-stager's desired behavior on a healthy day.

A one-line sibling test (`runGate('policy-missing', viewSeq: ['missing'], assets: ['fa-linux-x64.tar.gz'], env: {'RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP': '1'})` → exit 0 + `release upload` in the gh log) would keep a future refactor of the policy's placement from accidentally gating the missing-release flow — same spirit as the draft-path pin in this test.

All checks pass. The review is complete and the artifacts are written.

## Review Summary — PR #2051 (gh-2050: daily-publish cli leg failed)

**Verdict: APPROVE** (0 blocking, 0 important, 2 suggestions).

**What the PR does**: adds a fail-closed, caller-declared opt-in (`RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP=1`, exact-match) to the gh-2042 release immutability gate, converting the PUBLISHED + unattached-`fa-*` refusal into a loud whole-call skip (`::warning::`, exit 0, zero mutation) for the daily `release-macos` desktop pre-stager attach only. The CLI-tar/extension attaches and all `ci.yml` tag-train call sites keep the refusal.

**Verification performed** (grader-parity, neutral probes against the checked-out PR branch):
- 137 tests pass across the two changed suites + all 5 related release-pin suites (`release_hygiene`, `release_drift_workflow`, `gh1847_release_extension_train`, `ci_release_dedupe_guard`, `ci_1684_extension_size_gate`); `dart analyze` clean.
- 5 direct behavioral probes of the gate script: policy skip (exit 0 + warning, 0 uploads), default refusal (exit 1), `true` value refused (fail-closed), draft path unchanged (`--clobber` upload), already-attached immutable skip (no warning).
- Grep fallback for CodeGraph: all gate callers inventoried; env propagation through `release_attach_or_create.sh` confirmed; `fa.ipa` does **not** match the `fa-*` glob, so the mobile leg is not exposed (PR description note corrected in the general comment).
- Formatting drift on the test files is pre-existing on `origin/main` (old-style formatter vs Dart 3.7+ tall style) and not CI-gated — not introduced by this PR.

**Findings**: 💡 policy scopes only to the refused verdict — confirm the manifest-alone refresh path on the unchanged `uploadable` branch is intended (inline, gate line 108); 💡 missing a missing-release + policy pin test (inline, test line 198); out-of-diff: misleading "✅ attached N asset(s)" line after a zero-mutation skip, and the `fa.ipa` note correction.

**Outputs written**: `outputs/pr_review.json` (valid JSON, APPROVE, consistent census), `outputs/pr_review_general.md` (13 lines, Summary/Key Issues/Next Steps), `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md` + `comment2.md` (both anchors verified as diff-added lines; both 💡 SUGGESTION, no 🚨 markers — census cross-check clean). No `outputs/response.md`, per instructions.
